I am thinking about this year the same way I did last year. My 2 mu is small — I cannot afford a bad harvest because one season feeds me for months. So I stick with what works. I do wheat in winter and maize in summer, like everyone around here in Quzhou.

For the wheat, I plant an improved variety — the seed shop in town sells Jimai or Shimai type, and my neighbors get 450-500 kg per mu with it. I sow around October 10. Before sowing I spread compound fertilizer — one bag of 15-15-15, that is 50 kg, on my 2 mu, so 25 kg per mu as base. Then at the green-up stage in March I topdress urea, about 15 kg per mu. That gives roughly 14-15 kg nitrogen per mu total. I irrigate the well water three times: before winter, at jointing, and at grain filling. One spray for aphids and powdery mildew in April, usually enough. I plow with the tractor before sowing — rotary tilling is what the machine guy does here.

For the maize, I plant hybrid seed — Zhengdan or Xianyu type, whatever the dealer has fresh. After wheat harvest in June I do no-till direct seeding, just drop the seed in with the planter. I put about 20 kg compound fertilizer per mu as base, then topdress 15 kg urea per mu at the big trumpet stage in late July. So about 16 kg nitrogen per mu. I irrigate once or twice depending on rain — if July rains are good, only once at tasseling. One spray for corn borer. Yield usually 550 kg per mu, sometimes 600 in a good year.

I do not skimp on fertilizer. Saving 50 yuan on urea is not worth losing 100 kg of grain. My farm is only 2 mu, so total fertilizer cost is manageable — maybe 600-700 yuan for the year. I do all the work myself, no hired labor needed on 2 mu.
